verdict.summary: You can create a Notion public connection yourself with no business verification. An 'Any workspace' connection can be installed through OAuth without a Marketplace listing. Only a Marketplace listing needs Notion's review, which takes 5-10 business days. The main risks are choosing the installation scope, which can't be changed after creation, and a docs note saying the Authorization URL only fills in after you submit for review.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min (plus 1-3 hours if you also prepare a Marketplace listing)
verdict.approval_wait: None for OAuth installs. 5-10 business days if you want a Marketplace listing (optional).

gates.name: Public connection in your development workspace
gates.unlocks: You create the connection, get the client ID and secret, and authorize your own Notion account through Composio.
limits: You need to be a workspace owner. This is documented for internal connections and likely applies to public ones too.
180 requests/min per connection on non-Business plans, 600/min on Business and Enterprise. A separate per-workspace limit is shared by all connections.
Data source queries are limited to about 3 requests/sec per connection.

gates.name: Shared install link (unlisted, or 'Selected workspaces only')
gates.unlocks: Other users authorize the connection through its OAuth flow. Each user picks which pages to share. Notion has no formal test-user allowlist.
limits: Notion publishes no install cap or user count for unlisted public connections.
'Selected workspaces only' connections on Free workspaces with more than one member hit a lifetime cap of 1,000 blocks. After a 3-day grace period, block creation returns 403.
Access is per user and per page. Nothing is granted workspace-wide.
Enterprise admins can restrict which connections members may install.
The docs say the Authorization URL field fills in only after you submit for review. Check this in the portal.

gates.name: Any-workspace public connection (optional Marketplace listing)
gates.unlocks: Any Notion user in any workspace can install through OAuth. A listing adds discovery in the Notion Marketplace.
limits: Only 'Any workspace' connections can be listed.
A listing needs Notion's security review. Rejections can be for brand/trademark, quality, or baseline-criteria reasons, and you can resubmit.
Not covered by the Free workspace block cap.
gates.time_to_reach: Immediate for OAuth installs. 5-10 business days for a Marketplace listing.

steps.title: Confirm you are a workspace owner
steps.detail: Sign in to the Notion workspace you will use for development and check that you have the Workspace Owner role. Notion requires owner rights to create connections.
gotchas: The docs state the owner requirement for internal connections. Assume it also applies to public connections until the portal confirms.

steps.title: Open the Developer portal and create a connection
steps.detail: Go to app.notion.com/developers/connections (the old notion.so/my-integrations URL redirects here). In the Build section, click Create new connection. Enter a connection name and pick your development workspace.
gotchas: New connections start as internal. Follow the public-connection flow so you end up with OAuth credentials.
The portal only works in a signed-in browser with JavaScript enabled.

steps.title: Choose installation scope: Any workspace
steps.detail: Set Installation scope to 'Any workspace' unless you only ever need specific workspaces. This setting can't be changed later. Only 'Any workspace' connections can be listed on the Marketplace or avoid the Free workspace 1,000-block cap.
gotchas: If you pick 'Selected workspaces only' and later want broad installs, you have to create a new connection.

steps.title: Register the Composio redirect URI
steps.detail: In the redirect URIs field, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio Notion auth config. The redirect_uri in each authorize request has to match a registered URI.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Composio's documented default redirect URI and its newer callback path differ. Copy whatever your auth config actually shows.
If you register more than one redirect URI, the token request must include redirect_uri too.

steps.title: Select the minimum capabilities
steps.detail: Notion has no OAuth scope strings. Instead, enable capabilities on the connection: content read/update/insert, comment read/insert, and a user-information level. An agent can map your tool usage to the smallest set. Then you tick those boxes in the portal.
gotchas: If you change capabilities after users have authorized, they all have to authorize again.
Fewer capabilities make workspace admins more likely to allow the install.

steps.title: Copy the OAuth client ID and secret
steps.detail: Open the connection's Configuration tab and copy the OAuth client ID and OAuth client secret. Store the secret in a secrets manager.
gotchas: The docs say the Authorization URL field may stay empty until you submit for review. Composio builds its own authorize URL from your client ID, so you shouldn't need that field.

steps.title: Create a custom Composio auth config
steps.detail: In Composio, create a Notion (toolkit 'notion') OAuth2 auth config with your own credentials. Enter the client ID and secret, and leave scopes empty. Composio calls Notion's token endpoint with HTTP Basic credentials.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection and finish Notion's consent screen. In the page picker, choose a few pages. Then call a read endpoint to confirm access. The token response should include access_token, refresh_token, bot_id and workspace_id.
gotchas: A wrong or unknown client_id lands on Notion's install-integration page instead of returning an OAuth error to your redirect URI.
The connection only sees pages the user selected in the picker.

steps.title: Check token refresh and monitor health
steps.detail: Make sure every refresh saves the new refresh_token, because Notion rotates it each time. Watch the connection's Health tab in the Developer portal for blocked requests, client errors and 429s.

steps.title: Share the connection with other users
steps.detail: Let other users connect through your app's Composio flow. Each user authorizes separately and picks their own pages. No listing or review is needed to use the OAuth flow.
gotchas: Enterprise workspaces may block connections that aren't on their admin-approved list.
If installs fail because the Authorization URL hasn't been populated, you may need to submit the connection for review first. The docs don't confirm this.

steps.title: (Optional) Draft a Marketplace listing
steps.detail: Draft the listing: name, description, category, tags, images and logo, linked to your 'Any workspace' public connection. Check it against Notion's Connection Gallery Best Practices.

steps.title: (Optional) Submit the listing for review
steps.detail: Submit the draft from Listings > Connections in the Developer portal. It then moves to the Submitted section.

steps.title: (Optional) Wait for Notion's review
steps.detail: Notion says it replies by email within 5-10 business days and may run a security review. If rejected, fix the stated reason and resubmit.

requirements.item: Workspace owner role in the development workspace
requirements.detail: Required to create connections. Documented for internal connections and likely needed for public ones too.

requirements.item: Registered redirect URI matching Composio's callback
requirements.detail: The redirect_uri sent in the authorize request must match a registered URI. If several are registered, the token request must include it.
Each refresh returns a new refresh token that replaces the old one.
Set once at creation. Required for a Marketplace listing and to avoid the Free workspace block cap.
Name, description, category and tags, images and logo, and a linked public connection. Only needed if you want a listing.
Required before the connection appears on the Marketplace. Not needed for OAuth installs.

scopes.effect: Enabled in the portal's capabilities, not requested as a scope string. Limited to pages the user picks.
Write capabilities. No separate review is documented. Enable only if your tools write to Notion.
Comment capabilities, configured the same way as content capabilities.
Returns user names and profile images.
Most sensitive level because it exposes email addresses. No separate review is documented, but it may make admins less willing to install.
Existing users have to authorize again.

blockers.symptom: You can't create a connection in the Developer portal or Settings > Connections
blockers.fix: Ask a workspace owner to grant you the owner role, or use a workspace you own.

blockers.symptom: The Authorization URL field on the connection is empty
blockers.cause: Notion's docs say this field fills in only after a public connection is submitted for review.
blockers.fix: Composio builds the authorize URL from your client ID, so try connecting through Composio first. If installs fail, submit the connection for review.

blockers.symptom: You can't list the connection on the Marketplace, or a Free workspace hits block limits
blockers.cause: The connection was created with 'Selected workspaces only', which can't be changed.
blockers.fix: Create a new public connection with 'Any workspace' scope and move users over to it.

blockers.cause: A Free workspace with several members hit the 1,000 lifetime block cap (internal or selected-workspace connections). The 3-day grace period has ended.
blockers.fix: The workspace has to upgrade, or you switch to an Any-workspace public connection. Retrying won't help.

blockers.cause: Notion has restricted the connection's API access.
blockers.fix: Check the Health tab and contact Notion. Retrying won't help.

blockers.cause: The per-connection limit (180 or 600 per minute) or the shared per-workspace limit was exceeded.
Brand or trademark issues, quality concerns, or unmet baseline criteria.
blockers.fix: Fix the reason given in the email and resubmit from the portal.

blockers.symptom: Users in an Enterprise workspace can't install the connection
blockers.cause: The workspace admin restricts which connections members may install.
blockers.fix: Ask the workspace admin to add your connection to their approved list.

composio.note: Composio's managed Notion OAuth app is fine for development and testing. Notion has no scope strings: access comes from the capabilities set on the connection plus the pages each user picks. Register your own public connection if you want your own consent branding and client credentials, your own per-connection rate-limit budget, or a Marketplace listing. Create it with 'Any workspace' scope. Before registering the redirect URI, copy the exact callback URL your Composio auth config shows, because Composio's default and newer callback paths differ.

open_questions: Does the Authorization URL really need a review submission before other users can install? The docs link it to submission, but they also say OAuth works without a listing. It's unclear whether Composio's own authorize URL works before review.
Is owner rights required to create a public connection, or only internal ones?
Is there any install cap or user limit for unlisted, unreviewed public connections? None is published.
How long do access tokens last? Expiry isn't documented, though refresh rotation is.
Is PKCE supported? Only client-secret HTTP Basic auth is documented.
What are the review criteria for connection listings? The Connection Gallery Best Practices page was not retrieved.
What is the exact redirect URI Composio requires for a custom Notion auth config? Its default and newer callback paths differ.
Does a public connection need anything beyond owner status, such as a paid plan or business verification? None was found.
